video_title: 5 Takeaways From the NEW YORK KNICKS Championship Run! | NBA Finals

quotes.speaker: Cam Johnson
quotes.summary_phrase: San Antonio Spurs lacked the composure and experience to close out games
quotes.excerpt: there's a difference between that and having an end of game sort of philosophy, ideology, composure, poise
quotes.quote: Maybe they rely on having a 7-5 freak of nature and really athletic, really good players, but there's a difference between that and having an end of game sort of philosophy, ideology, composure, poise and thought process as a group that that experience brings. And so San Antonio just wasn't quite there yet.

quotes.speaker: Cam Johnson
quotes.summary_phrase: New York Knicks' veteran experience gave them the edge in close games
quotes.excerpt: I think the little bit of extra experience, age, all that stuff just gave them an edge
quotes.quote: Nothing was necessarily easy for them this series. It was a lot of gut-check wins and they just, I think the little bit of extra experience, age, all that stuff just gave them an edge and guys stepped up and made plays when they needed to and boom, three games won on the road.

quotes.speaker: Cam Johnson
quotes.summary_phrase: Jalen Brunson's ability to make big plays consistently throughout the finals
quotes.excerpt: Jalen Brunson, head of the snake, was consistently able to make big plays all finals
quotes.quote: Ultimately it came down to Jalen Brunson, head of the snake, was consistently able to make big plays all finals. Whether he had struggled that whole game or not, early in the series there was a couple tougher games, but big time plays late in the game.

quotes.speaker: Cam Johnson
quotes.summary_phrase: Jalen Brunson's 45-point performance in Game 5 secured the championship
quotes.excerpt: 45 of the 94 just went off and carried them to that championship
quotes.quote: Game 5, he takes them home, probably the most fitting end for them that I could think of. 45 of the 94 just went off and carried them to that championship and his ability to take over that game won them that game.

quotes.speaker: Cam Johnson
quotes.summary_phrase: Jalen Brunson's rare status as a 6-2 lead guard winning an NBA championship
quotes.excerpt: how many 6-2 lead point guards have led their team purely led their team as a 1A
quotes.quote: How many 6-2 lead point guards have led their team purely led their team as a 1A like this to an NBA championship and the list isn't that long. So he put himself in elite company.

quotes.speaker: Cam Johnson
quotes.summary_phrase: Jalen Brunson's tactical adjustment to attacking the rim when Victor Wembanyama sat
quotes.excerpt: As soon as Wembanyama goes out, he's attacking the rim, head on
quotes.quote: He was kind of more of a jump shooter when Wembanyama was out of the game. As soon as Wembanyama goes out, he's attacking the rim, head on. And because of that, he's giving the Spurs different looks and he settled into a rhythm and continued to settle into a rhythm and was able to continue to knock down big shots on the stretch.

quotes.speaker: Cam Johnson
quotes.summary_phrase: New York Knicks' roster depth and commitment to their roles
quotes.excerpt: They had guys that were just ready, able and willing to fill their role consistently
quotes.quote: They had guys that were just ready, able and willing to fill their role consistently. You knew what you were getting from everybody effort-wise, you knew what you were getting from everybody contribution-wise and it's just a roster where in this run, in this stretch of months, the pieces fit exactly the way they wanted it to to make them the best team.

quotes.speaker: Cam Johnson
quotes.summary_phrase: Jalen Brunson's Finals MVP performance and efficiency
quotes.excerpt: Finals MVP, well deserved. It was a big moment for him
quotes.quote: Finals MVP, well deserved. It was a big moment for him and I've heard this argument all day. Jalen Brunson, 45 of the 94, a pretty efficient outing with the two, but it's the way he was creating.

quotes.speaker: Cam Johnson
quotes.summary_phrase: New York Knicks' composure in high-pressure situations compared to the Spurs
quotes.excerpt: The Knicks looked really comfortable in what they were doing and the Spurs looked really uncomfortable
quotes.quote: When everything tightened up, when everything got a little bit more intense, when the game was actually on the line, the Knicks looked really comfortable in what they were doing and the Spurs looked really uncomfortable. The shots the Spurs were getting looked uncomfortable. The shots the Knicks were getting looked more comfortable.

quotes.speaker: Cam Johnson
quotes.summary_phrase: The inevitability of young teams struggling with high-pressure moments
quotes.excerpt: It happens to every team. The younger they are, NBA is talented and the talent is like this
quotes.quote: It happens to every team. The younger they are, NBA is talented and the talent is like this where some teams have a little bit more, some teams have a little bit less. I remember my rookie year, our Phoenix Suns group was a younger group overall and I remember thinking, dang, it's hard to win in the NBA.

quotes.speaker: Cam Johnson
quotes.summary_phrase: New York Knicks' growth and development into a championship-caliber team
quotes.excerpt: Our units, our groups, our whole team philosophy just grows over time
quotes.quote: Our units, our groups, our whole team philosophy just grows over time and we're the team that's winning in this fourth quarter, we're the team that's comfortable in this fourth quarter. And it's just something that can be grown, it's something that can be built.

quotes.speaker: Cam Johnson
quotes.summary_phrase: New York City as a foundational hub for basketball culture
quotes.excerpt: New York is inherently hoops, it's culture. It's a very big cultural hub for us
quotes.quote: New York is inherently hoops, it's culture. It's a very big cultural hub for us and it's a very big as much as they kind of haven't produced like top-end talent out of New York City in recent years, it's still like a foundation of hoop culture and hoop culture in America.

quotes.speaker: Cam Johnson
quotes.summary_phrase: The significance of the Knicks' championship for their fanbase
quotes.excerpt: 50 years without a championship puts a lot more emphasis on this one
quotes.quote: 50 years without a championship puts a lot more emphasis on this one, but the fact that the fanbase has remained solid, like it's been a known thing. It just kind of adds up to that. I'm not surprised that this would dwarf potentially any other New York championship.

quotes.speaker: Cam Johnson
quotes.summary_phrase: Mikal Bridges' impact and consistency as a teammate
quotes.excerpt: Mikal was a big part of my career early on. He does not miss anything
quotes.quote: Mikal was a big part of my career early on. He does not miss anything. He's always going to be on the court, he's always going to be at practice, he's always going to be at games, he's always he's always available and he got a lot of scrutiny early on in New York and they gave up a lot to get him, but it's got to be all worth it now.

quotes.speaker: Tommy Alter
quotes.summary_phrase: The Knicks' fanbase's resilience through years of struggle
quotes.excerpt: Even compared to the Yankees and the other sports teams in New York, because they have not had
quotes.quote: Even compared to the Yankees and the other sports teams in New York, because they have not had really any success and they've had a lot of, you know, rough moments over the last 15-20 years and the fact that they keep showing up and they keep, I remember I remember seeing the lottery parties when Zion was in the draft. You know, and there would be any any sliver of hope they could get that this was going to be this is sort of what has made this run so amazing.

quotes.speaker: Tommy Alter
quotes.summary_phrase: Comparing the Knicks' championship expectations to the Yankees
quotes.excerpt: I think the Lakers are more like the Yankees where they have an expectation for championships and success
quotes.quote: I think the Lakers are more like the Yankees where they have an expectation for championships and success and so they are if they have a mediocre team, they're less likely to put up with it. And what I would say is like you could make the argument that's they should be that way. I'm not even saying that's a bad thing. I'm just saying that what makes the Knicks so great is they're there no matter what.
